question: Add a recipient-side sensitivity tier to R5: for all 929 whitelisted recipients, replace the recipient's DAF share of total assets with its same-FY Schedule D DAF contributions / Part VIII line 1h total contributions (SOI extracts TY2021-24), and add a one-year lag variant for June-FYE grantors to December-FYE recipients; report FY2021-24 netted grants and payout under each
conclusion_affected: R5 central estimate and netted payout rate (22.3-25.2%)
rationale: For the 11 largest CF/single-issue recipients the contribution-share weight gives $4.80bn of FY2021-24 netting against $4.39bn central (+9%); the contribution share is lower for 5 of 11, and far lower only at PEF Israel (19.5% vs asset share 0.64). SVCF's FY2022 inbound lines equal 52% of its same-FY DAF contributions and 108% of next-FY, and 83% of its inbound dollars come from grantors with another FYE, so the timing match matters at the largest recipient

question: Confirm the 3 likely and 6 possible line-6 'No' sponsors found by the full-text screen outside NTEE T30/T31/T70 (Dakota Medical Charities, New Mexico Community Trust, Bayou Community Foundation; Sharp HealthCare Foundation, Greater Rochester Community Health Foundation, Miller-Dwan, Samaritan Bethany, Greater Gig Harbor, Starkey) from websites, fund agreements and next returns, and hand-read a sample of the 331 mention-only (class C) returns
conclusion_affected: Sponsor count outside DAFRC; size of the line-6 false-negative tail
rationale: Among 126,684 line-6 'No' returns of 501(c)(3) filers with >= $1m assets outside the batch-37 universe, only 3 read as likely sponsors ($103.6m total assets, no Schedule D Part I values) and 6 as possible; Part I values appear on 11 returns totalling $2.96m, mostly operating charities misusing the column. The tail adds sponsors, not money, but Dakota Medical Charities says it is 'home of ... more than 100 donor-advised funds' while answering line 6 'No'
